source_text: Vestes scissae, caput nudum, extra castra. Luctus peccati. Extra ecclesiae pacem qui immundus perseverat.
orientation: Origen is interpreting the Levitical rule about the leper's torn clothes and uncovered head, applying it to the sinner who remains unclean and outside the peace of the church.
pass_a_gloss: Clothes torn, head bare, outside the camp. Mourning of sin. Outside the peace of the church is he who remains unclean.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the Levitical exclusion, preserving the spatial and communal sense of separation.
Keeps the genitive force of peccati as the object or cause of mourning, matching the terse Latin.

choices.english: Outside the peace of the church
choices.why: Preserves the spatial metaphor and the genitive ecclesiae, tying the Levitical camp to the church's communion.
Perseverat carries the sense of continuing in a state, not a single act; 'remains' captures the ongoing condition.

bible_refs.note: Vestes scissae, caput nudum, extra castra

pass_b_english: Torn clothes, bare head, outside the camp. Mourning of sin. Outside the peace of the church he who remains unclean.

last_rejected.why: Latin luctus is 'mourning/grief for' not 'of'; ambiguous English hides Origen's point about mourning over sin.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Mourning of sin' is standard genitive rendering of 'Luctus peccati'; meaning is clear and within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: Outside the peace of the church he who remains unclean.
last_rejected.source_quote: Extra ecclesiae pacem qui immundus perseverat.
last_rejected.why: Missing main verb sense: 'perseverat' means 'persists/remains' as ongoing action, not static state; also awkward word order obscures subject.
last_rejected.fix: He who persists in uncleanness remains outside the peace of the church.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Remains' correctly conveys 'perseverat'; word order follows Latin source; no meaning lost or changed.
